full_judgment:
3. It is plaint case that suit land originally belongs to Amol Sing Bahadur, Sib Krishana Sing Bahadur, sons of la t Maharaj Pran Krishna Sing Bahadur, Maharaj Kumod Krishna, Nirod Chandra Sing, Nogendra Chandra Sing and Dijendra Chandra Sing sons of late Maharaj Krishana Singh Bahadur who were the CS recorded owners and possessor of the suit property and their names have been recorded in CS khatian 16842/13, CS dag No. 211 area of lands measuring 9342 Ajautangsha, in CS dag No. 212 area of land measuring 3480 Ajutangsh, CS dag No. 213 area of land 5900 Aujutangsh, CS dag No. 223/369 the area of land measuring 7080 Ajutangsha, CS dag No. 329 area of land measuring 2328 Ajutangsha. But in the suit claim was made for the land of CS dag No. 223/369 of area of land 7080 Ajutangsha. Out of this area of land, plaintiff's claim is for 473 Ajutangsha of land. The CS recorded owners paid rents and taxes of land in question to the concerned authority in time and enjoyed the same peacefully to the knowledge of all. Predecessor of plaintiff Sreemati Sarnalata Dey wife of, Srejukta Dinehs Chandra Dey became owner and possessor of the suit land from Sree Sudhindar Chandra Sing Sharma, Sree Shurid Chandra Sing Sharma, sons of late Promod Chandra Sing Sharma, Sreemati Surama Devi, wife of, late Promon Chandra Sing Sarnia, Sree Debesh Kumar Sing Sharma, Sree Somesh Kumar Sing Sharma, Sreemati Sibani Debi, wife of late Shudir Chandra Sing Sarma, Sree Surath Chandra Sing Sharma, Sere Suresh Chandra Sing Sharma sons of late Girindra Chandra Singh Sharma by registered deed of sale being No. 1495 dated 15-5-1941. Syed Ali Habib, son of late, Syed Abdul Latif become owner and possessor of the suit land from Sreemati Sarnalata Dey, wife of Sree Dinesh Chandra Dey by registered deed of perpetual lease being No. 4593 dated 30-9-1950 followed by registered deed of sale being No. 4594 dated 30-9-1950. The predecessor of the vendor and the vendor paid rents and taxes to the concerned authorities for the suit land. Before being alienated they possessed the land in question peacefully and after they divested themselves of the suit land, the vendees stepped into their shares and being bonafide owners in possession paid rents and taxes in time of the concerned authorities. Name of Syed Ali Habib, son of, Syed Abdul Latif was duly recorded in SA khatian No. Sabek 1328 Hal 804, SA dag No. 1800, area of land measuring 0473 Ajutangsha. Being bonafide owner in possession he paid Government rents, taxes of the suit land to the concerned authorities in time. Syed Ali Habib died leaving Syed Ali Azhar, Syed Ali Mazhar, Syed Ali Asgar and Syeda Khatun sons and wife respectively of the deceased who stepped into the shoes of Syed Ali Habib in the suit land by dint of inheritance. They being bonafide owners in possession of the suit land, sold the same by an indenture of sale to Abdul Majid, son of late, Nur Muhammad being registered deed No. 12222 dated 29-9-1960. Abdul Majid died on 20-10-1983 leaving Abdur Aziz, Abdur Rashid, Nazma Begum, and Panchi Bibi as his sons, daughters and wife respectively. Plaintiff field succession case NO. 947 of 1983 in the Court of district delegate 3rd Sub-ordinate Judge, Dhaka and got succession certificate on 2-4-1984 for drawing money deposited in different Banks in the name of deceased Abdul Majid. After the death of Abdul Majid, his aforesaid sons, daughters and wife became owner and possessor of the property as successor as per Muslim law of inheritance. Plaintiff No. 1 is the husband of the plaintiff No. 2. Plaintiff No. 1 purchased 0074 Ajutangsha from Mrs Panchi Bibi by registered deed of sale being No. 1064 dated 12-3-1992, at a valuable consideration and got possession thereof. Plaintiff further purchased 0086 Ajutangsha of land from Mrs Amena Begum by registered deed of sale being No. 1241 dated 30-3-1992 at a valuable consideration and got possession thereof. Plaintiff also purchased an area of land measuring 0086 Ajutangsha of land from Mrs Nazma Begum by registered deed of sale being No. 1242 dated 30-3-1992. Plaintiff No. 1 against purchased 0090 Ajutangsha of land from Abdul Aziz by registered deed No. 2084 dated 21-5-1992. Plaintiff No. 1 again purchased 0061 Ajutangsha of land from A.bdur Rashid by registered deed No. 2.312 dated 8-6-1992. Plaintiff No. 1 again purchased 0051 Ajutangsha of land from Abdul Aziz by registered deed No. 1901 dated 14-5-1998 at a valuable consideration and got possession thereof. Plaintiff No. 2 purchased 0061 Ajutangsha and 0051 Ajutangsha of land from Abdur Rashid and Abdur Aziz by registered deeds of sale being No. 2318 dated 8-6-1992 and No. 2005 dated 21-5-1992. 

 4. IN this way by 8 registered sale deeds plaintiffs became owner and possessor of three Katha nine chataks of land with structures standing thereon to the knowledge of all including the defendants. Plaintiffs mutuated their names and got mutated Parcha, rent receipt, DCR and where/are paying government land revenue and taxes in their names. But due to reason not known they realized rents from the plaintiffs for 0473 Ajutangsha of land. When objection raised to this, they were said that when Tasdik Parcha will be published finally they will realize rents from the plaintiffs accordingly. Their names were recorded in Tasdik Parcha for 0586 Ajutangsha of land, in Khatian No. 5257 DP 3432, Dag No. 5344, Mouia Wari, Police Station-Sutrapur, Dhaka. In the opinion column it is remarked that there is a 4(four) storied pucca building in possession of the plaintiffs. The names of the plaintiffs were duly recorded and mutated in Dhaka City Corporation and the plaintiffs have been allotted holding No. 16/1/A, Rankin Street, Dhaka and the plaintiffs have been paying holding taxes to the Dhaka City Corporation in time and they have enjoyed the suit property peacefully without any objection from anybody of are quarter whatsoever. 

 7. Defendant No. 1 contested the suit by filing written statement and in the written statement the plaint case was denied line by line and it is his specific case that predecessor of the plaintiffs purchased land from Sree Sarnalata Dey when Title Suit No. 141 of 1945 was pending and this purchase is hit by lis pendency, Plaintiffs filed Title Suit No. 171 of 1985 impleading Kaniz Fatema, predecessor of the defendant No. 1 Suit was dismissed. Plaintiffs filed Title Appeal No. 120 of 1957 and thereafter plaintiffs filed Appeal from Appellate Decree No. 195 of 1958 and these appeals were dismissed thereby title of Sarnalata, predecessor of the plaintiffs and also of the plaintiffs totally lost and extinguished. It is further case of this defendant that suit land originally belongs to Maharaj of Durgapur, Mymensingh and CS Khatian was prepared in the name of heirs of Maharaj Durgapur, Mymensingh who filed Partition Suit No. 145 of 1927 in the Court of Sub-ordinate Judge, 4th Court, Mymensingh and in that suit, sham for an area of 1475 Ajutangsha was allowed to Raja Shibkrishna Sing. For the remaining land of the aforesaid dag the other heirs who got saham, from them, Charulata Paul by registered deed No. 2369 dated 19-9-1938 purchased 4 kathas and 1 chha tak 6½ gandas of land and got possession and from Charulata Paul, Kaniz Fatema by registered deed No. 4113 in 1950 purchased the said land ands got possession. Direndra Chandra Sing and other 3 sons of raja Shibkrishna Sing also got 4/7 shares and for title and recovery of possession against Charulata Paul, Sarnalata Paul and others as plaintiffs filed Title Suit No. 141 of 1945 in the court of Sub-ordinate Judge, 1st Court, Dhaka renumbered before the court of additional Sub-ordinate Judge, Dhaka as Title Suit No. 40 of 1951. The suit was dismissed on 25-5-1951 and while the said suit was pending Sarnalata Paul sold some land to Syed Ali Habib. Sarnalata Dey did not get any land in the suit and by purchase from Sarnalata Dey, Syed Ali Habib also did not get any land as his purchase was hit by lis pendency. Kaniz Fatema, the predecessor of defendant purchased the decree of that suit on 22-4-1952 and replaced his name as decree holder and by executing decree through Title Execution case No. 66 of 1952 of Court of 5th Sub-ordinate Judge, Dhaka wherein Advocate Commissioners were appointed, got 0488 Ajutangsha of land and got possession by court on 25/8/1953 and demarcated by opening khatian No. 16842/13. The heirs of Syed Ai Habib filed Title Suit No. 171 of 1955 before the Munsif, 6th Court, Dhaka for declaration of title and for khash possession against the mother of this defendant, Kaniz Fatema as defendant. The suit was dismissed on 28-6-1957, against which Title Appeal No. 120 of 1957 was filed. Appeal was dismissed on 5-11-1957. Against which decision plaintiffs of that suit filed Appeal from Appellate Decree No. 195 of 1958 before the High Court Division. This appeal also dismissed by the High Court Division by judgment dated 25-8-1959. Against that decision, plaintiffs of that suit did not take any step as such, plaintiffs have no title over the suit property as they purchased the land from a person who had no title and possession over the suit land. In this way Kaniz Fatema by purchase became owner of 4 khathas 1 Chhatak = .0608 Ajutangsha of land and by decree got .1158 Ajutangsha of land. Later on, Kaniz Fatema sold .856 Ajutangsha of land to Lutfar Rahman and retain. 0302 Ajutangsha of land was is in her possession till her death. In the recent survey, the name of Kaniz Fatema was first recorded for 1022 Ajutangsha of land, later on, by deducting 0.056, Ajutangsha of land which was sold and recorded in the name of Lutfor Rahman, 0240 Ajutangsha of land was recorded in the name of Kaniz Fatema in khatian No. 5523 and 5520. It is further case of this defendant that in schedule dag of Kaniz Fatema, plaintiffs surreptitiously in Mutation Case No. 2177/1994-95 mutated their names of which defendant after came to know filed Miscellaneous Case No. 20/1997-98 which was allowed and recording of the name of the plaintiffs in Mutation Case No. 2177/1994-95 was cancelled on contested hearing. Against the decision of Miscellaneous Case No. 20/1997-98, Miscellaneous Appeal No. 112 of 2005 was filed before the Assistant Commis-sioner (Revenue), Dhaka which was also dismissed. Against that, Miscellaneous Appeal 18 of 2005 was filed before Additional Divisional Commissioner which was also dismissed. 

 8. Defendant No. 2-6 also contested the suit by filing written statement in which they have denied the case of plaintiff and it is their specific case that the suit land originally belonged to Hemendra Mohon Bashak and Copal Bashak and others; the suit land was enlisted in sensuous list leased out of Nirmal Chandra Bashak in EP Case 228 of 1967 and EP Case No. 11 of 1971. The original owner having left this country before 1947 without any maintenance of the suit land and without any person for looking the property to India, as such, SA khatian No. 1800 has been prepared accordingly and included the property in VP sensuous list and the suit land have been recorded in its 16 annas title and recorded in the Government correctly and RS and SA khatian also prepared in the name of Government as vested property as original owner left for India before 1947, as such, the suit property has been rightly declared as enemy property as vested property and Government having possession and its management, plaintiff can not claim title of vested property and the suit is liable to be dismissed with cost. 

 14. To answered the first question, we have gone through the depositions of the witnesses and Exhibits filed by the parties. It appears that plaintiffs Exhibited Exhibit 1, certified copy CS khatian, produced the deed of acquiring title from Sarnalata dey by which Syed Ali Habib in certified copy as exhibt 7, plaintiffs also produced Exhibit 8 which is the deed of 30-9-1952. Plaintiff produced Exhibit 8 and 9 by which Syed Ali Habib at first got pattan, lease and thereafter, purchased the land from Sarnalata Dey in certified copy, Plaintiff also produced Exhibit 9 to 18 i.e. deed of purchase of the plaintiffs in certified copy, plaintiffs did not produce any original deed. We do not find any explanation as to whereabouts of the originals of these deeds as such, an averse presumption may be drawn against the plaintiffs. 

 18. Next we have seen that Exhibit filed by the parties. It appears from Exhibit 'Uma' khatian No. 870/1 the suit land recorded in the name of defendant and from Exhibit `Cha' enquiry report shows that the defendants are in possession. From Exhibit `Cha' Fazlur Rahman plaintiff claimed he got mutation of .0473 Ajutangsha of land but he has found in possession of 0.0006 Ajutangsha of land. From Exhibit `Chha' it appears that plaintiffs appeal being time barred was rejected and also Assistant Commissioner found that mutation in favour of plaintiff was done contradictory to the decision of the High Court Division passed in Second Appeal No. 195 of 1998. Exhibit 'Ja' is decision of Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) dismissing Miscellaneous Appeal No. 18 of 2005 filed by the plaintiff. Exhibit 'Ja-1' is Miscellaneous Appeal No. 18 of 2005 filed by the plaintiff and exhibt 'Jha' is the power of attorney.
